items.stimulus: In 1947, botanist Katherine Esau published Anatomy of Seed Plants, a textbook that helped establish plant anatomy as a distinct field of study. Esau combined microscopic observations with clear diagrams, <u>allowing students to see how tissues were organized within stems and leaves</u>. Her approach was especially valuable because it turned a complicated subject into something students could actually get their heads around. Although later researchers developed new imaging techniques, Esau's emphasis on careful observation remains relevant to botanical education. Today, historians of science regard her textbook as an important contribution to the field.

Manufacturers now use Kevlar in all kinds of products, from protective vests to marine cables. The material's strength comes from the arrangement of its long molecular chains, which align when the polymer is spun into fibers. Although Kwolek received numerous awards for her work, she continued to emphasize the contributions of the technicians who helped test the material. Her research demonstrates how an unexpected result in a laboratory can lead to practical advances in several industries.

Which is the best version of the underlined portion?
choices: was a significant development in materials science
was totally awesome for materials science
was an important and significant development for materials science
items.stimulus: While working at DuPont in 1964, chemist Stephanie Kwolek developed a liquid polymer solution with unusual properties. The solution looked cloudy and unremarkable, but a technician spun it into fibers for further testing. Those fibers proved to be exceptionally strong while remaining lighter than steel. DuPont introduced the material, later named Kevlar, in 1971 for use in specialized equipment. Kwolek's discovery <u>was a big deal for materials science</u>.
items.explanation: The surrounding passage uses a formal, informative register, so “was a significant development in materials science” is the most appropriate choice. “Big deal” and “totally awesome” are informal, while “important and significant” is redundant.
